defaults.teacher_persona: A network engineer who draws the path a packet actually takes before naming any device, and who reaches for the command line rather than the manual.
classmates: A service-desk technician moving up from desktop support and new to managed switches
A junior sysadmin who has inherited a Windows domain and a Linux box and is unsure which tool answers which question
defaults.interaction: Diagnostic: the teacher poses a failure, the classmates propose where to look, and the group narrows it down layer by layer until the command that proves it is named.
defaults.assessment: Each classroom ends with 3-5 checks aligned to the chapter's graded activity.

classrooms.title: Describing a Network Before You Touch It
classrooms.prompt: Run a session on how support work describes a network: size (LAN/WAN), topology, and the layer that carries the data. Give the classmates a site description and have them classify it, then trace one request from a laptop to an internet service and name the layer each hop belongs to.
objectives: Classify a network by size, topology, and the layers that carry data
Place a fault at a layer instead of guessing at a device
Walk a request end to end and name each hop

classrooms.title: Frames, Packets, and the Wireless Middle
classrooms.prompt: Contrast switching, routing, and wireless access, then debug a network where one VLAN cannot reach a printer on another. Have the classmates interpret a switch MAC table, an ARP cache, and a routing table in turn, and decide which one is actually wrong.
objectives: Explain what a switch, a router, and an access point each decide
Read a VLAN, MAC table, and routing table well enough to localise a fault
Diagnose a wireless client that associates but cannot reach anything

activities.title: One VLAN cannot reach the printer

classrooms.title: The Domain Is the Backbone
classrooms.prompt: Work through Active Directory Domain Services as the identity and policy backbone: domain controllers, DNS, DHCP, file shares, and Group Policy. Then have the classmates troubleshoot a user who cannot log in, separating a DNS problem from a replication problem from a locked account, using the tools an admin would actually run.
objectives: Describe the AD DS pieces and what each one is responsible for
Explain how DNS, DHCP, and Group Policy hang off the domain
Work a domain sign-in failure in the right order

activities.title: The user who cannot log in

classrooms.title: The Shell and the Service Model
classrooms.prompt: Teach Linux server administration through the shell and systemd: navigate the filesystem, read logs, and manage a service. Then run a short incident where nginx is not serving, and have the classmates use systemctl and journalctl to prove whether the unit, the port, or the config is at fault.
objectives: Navigate the Linux filesystem and read the logs that matter
Manage services with systemd instead of ad-hoc restarts
Diagnose a failed web service from status, journal, and socket
